title: Evaluation of Liquid Biopsy and cerebral biomarkers in diagnosis of Sturge-Weber Syndrome: a pilot study
summary: Our study evaluates whether the new laboratory method "liquid biopsy" may be used for a rapid, early diagnosis of Sturge-Weber Syndrome. The liquid biopsy simply means for the patient that a normal venous blood sample is drawn. Possibly, liquid biopsy may detect the causative GNAQ mutation for Sturge-Weber Syndrome in a blood sample. This would enable an early, rapid diagnosis in persons at risk for SWS, e.g. in persons with a large facial birthmark, and shorten a otherwise longer period of diagnostic uncertainty. In the same blood sample, we will analyse cerebral biomarkers. Ultimately, the combination of both tests could enable an early, rapid diagnosis of Sturge-Weber Syndrome through a blood test. An early diagnosis of Sturge-Weber Syndrome, prior to epilepsy onset, could enable especially administration of prophylactic antiseizure medications.

interventions.name: In 20 patients with Sturge-Weber Syndrome, diagnosis verified through MR tomography and clinically: we draw a venous blood sample, take a sample with saliva and oral mucosal cells, do a focussed clinical exam and the patients fill in an electronic questionnaire

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. clinically diagnosed Sturge-Weber Syndrome type 1, diagnosis made by a board certified physician (any specialty) 
2. primary residence in Germany
3.suspected Sturge-Weber Syndrome: inclusion and analysis separately
Exclusion criteria:
1. parents/ patients with insufficient knowledge of German language (< niveau A1)
2. known coagulation disorder
